newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Police arrest 100 at Zurich May Day demonstrations.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 100 at Zurich May Day demonstrations.

text.p: Zurich police said on Thursday they arrested about 100 demonstrators when May Day celebrations turned violent.
They said they also confiscated Molotov cocktails and objects which could be used as weapons from young members of a far-left group.

Earlier in the day several hundred police had been out in the city streets in an effort to contain traditional but illegal demonstrations that followed legal May 1 festivities attended by up to 5,000 people.
They used water cannon and rubber bullets to prevent around 500 demonstrators, some wearing masks and carrying placards with left-wing slogans, from marching into Zurich's business district.
The demonstrators hurled paint-filled balloons, rocks and bottles on their breakaway march.
Police in Zurich also refused to allow a planned speech by Isaac Velazco, European representative of the Peruvian rebel group, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
Velazco stood silent on the podium while a pre-recorded greeting was played on a cassette tape.

In a copy of his speech made available to Reuters, Velazco recalled labour struggles in Peru, and the part played in them by rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, killed in the April 22 raid to free 72 hostages held in Lima by the rebels.
